os-blazor.title: Blazor kit
os-blazor.summary: Ready-made Blazor components and services: buttons, fields, dialogs, themes and an API client, all set up with one call.

gives.1: Controls that work in both right-to-left and left-to-right layouts.
gives.2: Light and dark themes that are remembered between visits.
gives.3: One `AddOSBlazor` call that sets up `OS.Locale` too.

setup.title: Setup
setup.summary: One call registers the services, texts and options the controls need.

1.title: One registration
1.text: `AddOSBlazor` registers everything the controls use.

2.title: Shared base
2.text: Every control inherits `OSComponent`, so it takes `Class` and `Extra`.

3.title: API helpers
3.text: `ApiClient` and `TokenStore` help you call a JSON API.

4.title: Token storage
4.text: The token stays in session storage by default.

1.title: What gets registered
1.text:
`AddOSBlazor` registers what every control uses: `ThemeService`, `ShellService`, the toast service, the API client and `OS.Locale` with its translated text.

Pass an action to change the theme storage key, the icon sprite or the shell's starting state.

2.title: Class and Extra
2.text: All controls inherit `OSComponent`. So each one accepts `Class` for your own CSS classes and `Extra` for any other HTML attribute.

3.title: API and token
3.text:
`ApiClient` and `TokenStore` are small helpers for a JSON API.

The token is kept in session storage by default. In production, prefer an HttpOnly cookie behind your own backend.

register.title: Register the library
register.note: Call it once at startup. A second call does nothing, so shared setup code can call it safely.

texts.title: Add your own texts
texts.note: The library's texts are added first, so keys in your files override them.

own-locale.title: Set up OS.Locale yourself
own-locale.note: When you call `AddOSLocale` before `AddOSBlazor`, add the library's texts to your own options, otherwise the dialog texts stay empty.

type.BlazorOptions: Everything you can change at startup: locale, API, token, icons, theme and shell.
type.OSComponent: The base of every control. It adds `Class` and `Extra` so you never have to wrap a control just to style it.
type.IconOptions: Where the icon sprite lives and which prefix its icons use.
type.ThemeOptions: The storage key and the attribute values used for light and dark.
type.ApiClient: Sends JSON requests, adds the token and returns an `ApiResult`. Network and server failures come back as results, not as exceptions.
type.TokenStore: Keeps the access token and its expiry for `ApiClient`.

BlazorDI.AddOSBlazor: Registers the services, options and texts once; a second call does nothing.

shell.title: Shell and layout
shell.summary: The page frame: header, sidebar, body, footer and the navigation inside them.

1.title: App setup
1.text: `OSApp` sets up routing, the layout and an error page.

2.title: Page frame
2.text: `OSShell` is the frame, and you fill its regions yourself.

1.title: The frame
1.text:
`OSApp` sets up routing, the layout and an error page.

`OSShell` is the frame the layout draws. You fill its regions with `OSHeader`, `OSSidebar`, `OSBody`, `OSFooter` and `OSTabBar`. `OSHeader` is split into start, center and end.

2.title: Sidebar and drawer
2.text:
Put `OSNav`, `OSNavSection` and `OSNavLink` in the sidebar.

`ShellService` remembers whether the side rail is open. It also controls the drawer used on small screens.

3.title: Pages
3.text:
Pages inherit `OSPage`, which shows a toast when something fails.

Or they inherit `OSPanel`, which loads its data and tracks the busy and error state.

Both give you `Api`, the translated text `L` and the current culture profile.

rail.title: Open and close the sidebar
rail.note: `InitAsync` reads the saved state once. The rail's state is remembered between visits; the drawer is not.

layout.title: An app layout
layout.note: Regions are claimed by the shell, so their order inside it does not matter.

type.OSApp: Router, layout and error page in one component. Give it the assembly that holds your pages.
type.OSShell: The frame of the app. Its regions are the child components you place inside it.
type.OSSidebar: The side area. `Placement`, `Side` and `DrawerEdge` decide where it sits on large and small screens.
type.OSNavLink: A sidebar link with an icon that marks the current page.
type.OSPage: Base class for pages. `Failed` shows an error toast.
type.OSPanel: Base class for parts of a page that load their own data. Override `ReloadAsync`.
type.OSView: A plain base for views that only need `Api`, `L` and the culture.
type.ShellService: The state of the side rail and the drawer.
type.ShellOptions: Whether the rail starts open and the key it is saved under.

ShellService.ToggleRailAsync: Opens or closes the rail and saves the choice.
ShellService.ToggleDrawer: Opens or closes the drawer used on small screens.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.summary: Buttons that act, link, copy and pick files.

1.title: Button or link
1.text: Give a button `Href` and it becomes a link; otherwise it raises `OnClick`.

2.title: Look
2.text: `ButtonKind` and `ButtonSize` set the look.

1.title: Buttons and links
1.text:
`OSButton` and `OSIconButton` share one base. Give them `Href` and they render as a link, with `Target` when needed. Otherwise they raise `OnClick`.

`ButtonKind` and `ButtonSize` set the look.

2.title: Copy and files
2.text:
`OSCopyButton` copies `Text`, or whatever `TextFactory` returns, and shows `DoneLabel` for a moment.

`OSFileButton` saves a text as a file. `OSFilePicker` opens the file dialog.

When the file passes `MaxBytes`, it reports `OnTooBig` instead of `OnPick`.

actions.title: Buttons and links
actions.note: `Kind` sets the look. With `Href` a button becomes a link.

copy-and-save.title: Copy text and save a file
copy-and-save.note: Both buttons show a short confirmation by themselves.

picker.title: Pick a file with a size limit
picker.note: `OnTooBig` runs instead of `OnPick` when the file is larger than `MaxBytes`.

type.OSButton: A text button with an optional icon.
type.OSIconButton: An icon-only button. `Label` is required because it becomes the accessible name.
type.OSCopyButton: Copies text to the clipboard. Use `TextFactory` when the text must be built at click time.
type.OSFilePicker: Lets the user pick one file and checks its size first.

fields.title: Fields
fields.summary: Text, search, choice and dropdown inputs with labels, hints and errors.

1.title: Shared options
1.text: Every field takes `Label`, `Hint`, `Error`, `Required` and `Disabled`.

2.title: List fields
2.text: The four list fields share one shape and take `Items`.

4.title: Image and search
4.text: `OSImageField` handles a picture and `OSSearchField` gives you the search text.

1.title: Shared options
1.text: Every field takes `Label`, `Hint`, `Error`, `Required` and `Disabled`. `OSFieldFrame` draws them the same way everywhere.

2.title: List fields
2.text:
`OSSelectField`, `OSChoiceField`, `OSDropdown` and `OSMultiDropdown` share one shape. Pass `Items`.

Then tell the field how to read an item with `TextOf` and `KeyOf`. `DisabledOf` turns single items off.

3.title: Switch, image, search
3.text:
`OSSwitch` is a boolean.

`OSImageField` previews, picks and removes a picture. `OSSearchField` raises `OnSearch` with the text.

text.title: Text, password and search
text.note: `Error` shows under the field and turns it red.

lists.title: Select, choice and multi-select
lists.note: All three read their items the same way: `Items`, `TextOf` and `KeyOf`.

switch.title: An on/off switch
switch.note: `OnText` and `OffText` show next to the switch.

type.OSTextField: Single-line input. `Type` also covers passwords, with a show/hide button.
type.OSSearchField: Text input with a search icon and a clear button.
type.OSSelectField{TValue}: A native select. `GroupOf` groups the items and `BlankText` adds an empty choice.
type.OSChoiceField{TValue}: Pick one item from a visible list of radio choices. `NoneText` adds a choice for nothing, and `Clearable` lets the user undo a pick.
type.OSSwitch: An on/off switch bound to a `bool`.
type.OSImageField: Shows a picture with buttons to pick, replace and remove it. You handle the upload.
type.OSDropdown{TValue}: A dropdown for one value, with an `ItemTemplate` for custom rows.
type.OSMultiDropdown{TValue}: A dropdown for several values at once, bound to `Values`.
type.OSFieldFrame: The label, hint and error around a field. Use it to build your own field.

display.title: Display
display.summary: Cards, chips, labels, icons, page headers and code.

1.title: Cards
1.text: `OSCard` is a titled block and `OSStatCard` shows a number with its change.

2.title: Chips
2.text: `OSChip` and `OSStatusChip` show a short state in color.

3.title: Icons and marks
3.text: `OSIcon` draws an icon by name and `OSMark` is a small mark.

4.title: Code
4.text: `OSCodeBlock` shows code with a copy button.

1.title: Cards, chips and icons
1.text:
`OSCard` is a titled block and `OSStatCard` shows a number with its change.

`OSChip` and `OSStatusChip` show a short state in one of the `ChipTone` colors. `OSIcon` draws a sprite icon by name. `OSMark` is a small mark with text or an icon.

2.title: Page head
2.text: `OSPageHead` is the title row of a page. Its `Details` slot takes `OSHeadItem` rows.

3.title: Code and inline text
3.text:
`OSCodeBlock` shows code with a copy button and an optional output. It is colored by an `ICodeHighlighter`, and C# is built in.

`OSInlineText` renders text written between backticks as separate left-to-right code. This keeps names like `IHook<TEvent>` readable inside Persian sentences.

cards.title: Cards, chips and stats
cards.note: `Tone` colors a chip. A stat card takes its direction from `Up`.

head.title: A page head
head.note: `Actions` sits at the end of the title row and `Details` holds the `OSHeadItem` rows.

code.title: Code with output, and inline code
code.note: `OSCodeBlock` colors C# only; any other `Language` is shown as plain text.

type.OSCard: A titled block with optional actions.
type.OSStatCard: A label, a value and a change, colored by `StatTone`.
type.OSChip: A small pill. It becomes a link with `Href` or a button with `OnClick`.
type.OSStatusChip: A chip that only shows a state; its tone carries the meaning.
type.OSIcon: Draws one icon from the sprite set in `IconOptions`.
type.OSPageHead: Title, subtitle, actions and a row of details at the top of a page.
type.OSHeadItem: One label and value pair inside `OSPageHead`.
type.OSCodeBlock: Code with a copy button, a language and an optional output below it.
type.OSInlineText: Plain text where `backtick` parts become inline code.
type.ICodeHighlighter: Turns code into colored HTML. Register your own to support another language.

overlays.title: Dialogs and messages
overlays.summary: Dialogs, confirmations, toasts, tooltips and menus.

1.title: Dialog
1.text: `OSDialog` is a modal window with a footer.

2.title: Toasts
2.text: Put one `OSToastHost` in the layout to show toasts.

3.title: Tooltip
3.text: `OSTooltip` shows a text next to its content.

4.title: Menu
4.text: `OSMenu` opens a list of rows from a button.

1.title: Dialog and confirm
1.text: `OSDialog` is a modal window with a footer. `OSConfirm` is the ready-made yes/no version.

2.title: Toasts
2.text:
Toasts need one `OSToastHost` in the layout.

After that, any component can inject `IToastService` and call `Good`, `Warn` or `Bad`.

3.title: Tooltip and menu
3.text:
`OSTooltip` wraps content and shows a text on the chosen `TooltipSide`.

`OSMenu` opens a list of `OSMenuItem` rows from a button. `OSMenuRule` is the divider.

notify.title: Show a message
notify.note: Messages disappear on their own. Calls with an empty text are ignored.

dialogs.title: A dialog and a confirmation
dialogs.note: Both bind `Open`. `OnYes` of the confirmation runs only when the user agrees.

menu-and-tip.title: A menu and a tooltip
menu-and-tip.note: `Danger` marks the destructive item; `OSMenuRule` draws the divider.

toast-host.title: Show toasts
toast-host.note: One `OSToastHost` in the layout is enough for the whole app.

type.OSDialog: A modal window. Bind `Open` and fill `ChildContent` and `Footer`.
type.OSConfirm: A yes/no question. `OnYes` runs when the user agrees and `Busy` disables the buttons meanwhile.
type.OSToastHost: Draws the toasts. Place one in the layout.
type.IToastService: What components inject to show a message.
type.OSTooltip: Shows a small text next to the wrapped content on hover or focus.
type.OSMenu: A button that opens a list of actions.
type.OSMenuItem: One row of a menu. `Danger` marks destructive actions.

IToastService.Show: Shows a message in any `ChipTone`, with an optional duration.

navigation.title: Navigation
navigation.summary: Tabs, accordions, trees, pagers and shortcuts.

1.title: Tabs
1.text: `OSTabs` shows one panel at a time.

2.title: Accordion
2.text: `OSAccordion` has sections that open one at a time or several at once.

1.title: Tabs and accordion
1.text:
`OSTabs` shows one panel at a time for a list of items.

`OSAccordion` holds `OSAccordionItem` sections, with one or several open at once. It also holds `OSAccordionLeaf` rows that behave as links.

2.title: Tree and icon bar
2.text:
`OSTree` draws nested items. Tell it where the children are with `ChildrenOf`.

`OSIconNav` is a compact icon bar.

3.title: Pager and back to top
3.text:
`OSPager` moves between pages and can offer page sizes.

`OSToTop` appears after scrolling and brings the user back to the top.

accordion.title: An accordion
accordion.note: `OpenId` is the id of the open section. Leaves link instead of opening.

tree.title: A tree
tree.note: `ChildrenOf` tells the tree where the children are; `Row` draws each item.

pager.title: A pager with page sizes
pager.note: The pager only reports the choice; you load the page.

type.OSTabs{TValue}: Tabs for a list of items. Bind `Value` to the selected item.
type.OSAccordion: A group of collapsible sections. `Multiple` lets several stay open.
type.OSAccordionItem: A section with a title, optional summary and actions, and a body.
type.OSAccordionLeaf: A row inside an accordion that links somewhere instead of opening.
type.OSTree{TItem}: A tree built from `Items` and `ChildrenOf`, with your own `Row` template.
type.OSIconNav: A bar of icon buttons built from `IconNavItem` entries.
type.OSPager: Page buttons with an optional page-size picker.
type.OSToTop: A button that scrolls to the top once the page has moved past `Threshold`.

data.title: Data views
data.summary: Grids, boards, loading states and the helpers that feed them.

1.title: Data grid
1.text: `OSDataGrid<T>` handles sorting, search and paging for you.

2.title: Group board
2.text: `OSGroupBoard` shows items under group headings.

3.title: Content states
3.text: `OSDataState` covers the waiting, empty and failed cases.

4.title: Server-side lists
4.text: `OSDataSet<T>` keeps the query and rows of a server-side list.

1.title: Grid and board
1.text:
`OSDataGrid<T>` shows rows through `OSColumn<T>` columns. It handles sorting, search, paging and CSV export for you.

`OSGroupBoard` shows items under group headings, with search and views.

2.title: Waiting and errors
2.text:
`OSDataState` covers the waiting, empty and failed cases of any content.

`OSBoundary` catches exceptions thrown while rendering.

3.title: Data set and editor
3.text:
`OSDataSet<T>` keeps the query and the rows of a server-side list. The query holds page, size, search, sort and criteria.

`OSEditor<TDraft>` does the same for a form. It keeps the draft, required fields, saving and the errors the server sends back.

dataset.title: Load a server-side list
dataset.note: The set cancels a request that is still running when a new one starts, so fast typing never shows old rows.

validate.title: Check a required field
validate.note: `Require` records an error for the field; `SaveAsync` will not call the server while any error is recorded.

grid.title: A data grid
grid.note: `Name` is the key used for sorting. Search and CSV export work on what `Text` returns.

state.title: Loading, empty and error states
state.note: The content shows only when none of the three applies.

type.OSDataGrid{T}: A table with sorting, search, paging and export. Fill it with `OSColumn<T>` entries.
type.OSColumn{T}: One column: `Title`, `Name` for sorting, and a `Template` or `Text` for the cell.
type.OSGroupBoard{TGroup,TItem}: Items grouped under headings, with search and switchable views.
type.OSDataState: Shows a spinner or skeleton, an empty message, an error or your content, whichever fits.
type.OSBoundary: Catches errors from its content and offers a retry. It recovers on its own when the user navigates.
type.OSDataSet{T}: The query and rows of a paged list, ready to bind to a grid and a pager.
type.OSEditor{TDraft}: The state of an edit form: the draft, errors, busy flag and save.
type.OSLoader: A larger loading indicator for whole sections.

OSDataSet{T}.SearchAsync: Waits a moment for more typing before it asks the server.
OSDataSet{T}.SortAsync: Sorts by the column and flips the direction when the same column is chosen again.

OSEditor{TDraft}.Require: Records an error for the field when the value is missing.
OSEditor{TDraft}.SaveAsync: Returns false without calling the server while an error is recorded. On success it closes the editor.

jobs.title: Long-running jobs
jobs.summary: A dialog that plans, runs, watches and stops a job on the server.

1.title: Step by step
1.text: `OSJobDialog<TPlan,TResult>` walks a long job through its steps.

2.title: Server source
2.text: It reaches the server through `IJobSource`.

4.title: Lost connection
4.text: After three failed status reads, the dialog says the connection is lost.

1.title: How it runs
1.text:
`OSJobDialog<TPlan,TResult>` walks a long job through its steps. It first shows the plan and starts the job.

Then it polls the status and offers Stop. Finally it shows the result or a file to download.

2.title: Server access
2.text:
The dialog reaches the server through `IJobSource`. `HttpJobSource` is the ready-made one.

It uses `GET`, `GET /plan`, `POST` and `DELETE` on a single path.

3.title: Texts and lost connection
3.text:
Texts come from the shipped translations, and `OSJobTexts` changes any of them. A value of `null` keeps the shipped text and an empty string hides that part.

If the status cannot be read three times in a row, the dialog says the connection is lost and polls less often.

source.title: Use your own job source
source.note: Anything that can answer these four calls works: a SignalR hub, a queue or a job running inside the app.

texts.title: Change some texts
texts.note: Properties you leave out keep the shipped, translated text.

progress.title: Read the progress
progress.note: `Percent` is rounded and is 0 while the total is unknown.

dialog.title: A job dialog
dialog.note: `Path` builds an `HttpJobSource`. Give `Source` instead to use your own.

type.OSJobDialog{TPlan,TResult}: The dialog. Give it `Path` or a `Source`, templates for the plan and the result, and `OnDone`.
type.OSJobStatus: What the server reports: state, phase, progress, time, message, result and an optional file.
type.OSJobState: Idle, running, done, failed or cancelled.
type.OSJobTexts: Optional overrides for every text in the dialog.
type.IJobSource: The four calls the dialog needs: status, plan, start and stop.

OSJobStatus.Percent: Done as a percentage of Total, rounded.

IJobSource.PlanAsync: Returns what the job is about to do, shown before the user starts it.

themes.title: Themes and styles
themes.summary: Light, dark and system themes, and the design tokens behind them.

1.title: Theme mode
1.text: `ThemeService` keeps the chosen theme in browser storage.

2.title: Toggle button
2.text: `OSThemeToggle` is the ready-made button for switching themes.

3.title: CSS variables
3.text: Colors, spacing and the font come from CSS variables.

4.title: Style layer
4.text: Control styles live in the `os.ctrls` layer, so your own CSS wins without `!important`.

1.title: Theme mode
1.text:
`ThemeService` keeps the chosen mode in browser storage, applies it to the page and tells you when it changes. The mode is `ThemeMode`: system, light or dark.

`OSThemeToggle` is the ready-made button for it.

2.title: Variables and fonts
2.text: Colors, spacing and the font come from CSS variables such as `--os-font`. The library ships no fonts, so set that variable in your own CSS.

3.title: Style layer
3.text: All control styles live in the `os.ctrls` CSS layer. So your own unlayered CSS wins without `!important`.

names.title: Rename the theme values
names.note: The attribute and its two values are what your own CSS selects on.

switch.title: Change the theme from code
switch.note: In system mode the page follows the device and updates when the device switches.

toggle.title: A theme toggle
toggle.note: `IncludeSystem` adds a third choice that follows the device.

type.ThemeService: The current mode and whether the page is dark right now.
type.OSThemeToggle: A button that switches between light and dark, optionally with a system choice.

ThemeService.ToggleAsync: Switches between light and dark based on what the page shows now.
ThemeService.Changed: Raised after the theme is applied.
